cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator / Full Time Holiday Contract University Town Center, Sarasota — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / Full Time Holiday Contract University Town Center, Sarasota opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Vision Hospitality Group, Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Guest Service Representative (Rotating Shifts FT & PT) opportunity with Vision Hospitality Group, Inc. at Vision Hospitality Group, Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Genetic Research Data Analyst (18-Month Fixed-Term, Hybrid Opportunity) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Stanford University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Genetic Research Data Analyst (18-Month Fixed-Term, Hybrid Opportunity) opportunity with Stanford University at Stanford University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Spacecraft Propulsion Components Engineer I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Rocket Lab Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Spacecraft Propulsion Components Engineer I opportunity with Rocket Lab at Rocket Lab.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Administrative Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Princeton University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Assistant opportunity with Princeton University at Princeton University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Oregon Charter Academy Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Administrative Assistant - School Enrollment Specialist 1 opportunity with Oregon Charter Academy at Oregon Charter Academy.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Computer Systems Support Administrator I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Institute for Defense Analyses Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Computer Systems Support Administrator I opportunity with Institute for Defense Analyses at Institute for Defense Analyses.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Research Coordinator I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Fred Hutch Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Research Coordinator I opportunity with Fred Hutch at Fred Hutch.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Data Specialist - Genitourinary Oncology (GU) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Data Specialist - Genitourinary Oncology (GU) opportunity with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Assistant I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear CenExel Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Assistant I opportunity with CenExel at CenExel.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Dear Barnes-Jewish Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Labor & Delivery Unit Secretary-PRN opportunity with Barnes-Jewish Hospital at Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Learning & Development Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Solar Turbines Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Learning & Development Coordinator opportunity with Solar Turbines at Solar Turbines.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in RESEARCH ASST I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Loyola University Chicago Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the RESEARCH ASST I opportunity with Loyola University Chicago at Loyola University Chicago.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Data Specialist - Genitourinary Oncology (GU) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Data Specialist - Genitourinary Oncology (GU) opportunity with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Instructional Designer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear CKE Restaurants, Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Instructional Designer opportunity with CKE Restaurants, Inc. at CKE Restaurants, Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Behavior Analyst in Training - North Mountain Village — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Soar Autism Center Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Behavior Analyst in Training - North Mountain Village opportunity with Soar Autism Center at Soar Autism Center.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Security Engineer Intern
jobs.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions This is a 12-week internship during summer 2027. Coinbase’s Application Security team is rethinking how offensive security works. We use frontier AI models to find vulnerabilities at scale, red team our own AI systems, and automate the parts of security work that don't need a human. As an intern, you'll join that effort on a scoped project and see your work used in real security decisions. What you'll do: Build and test tooling that uses frontier AI models to surface vulnerabilities across Coinbase’s products, working alongside senior engineers on design and review. Help red team internal AI systems - probing for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and tool misuse, then documenting what you find and how to fix it. Automate pieces of the vulnerability triage, validation and remediation workflows so the bug bounty, vulnerability response pipelines move faster and become AI native. Reproduce and verify reported vulnerabilities across common classes (OWASP Top 10, SANS Top 25), and write findings that engineering partners can act on. Practice responsible AI use: keep a human in the loop, measure whether your tooling actually improves speed or quality, and be honest when it doesn’t. Required Skills and Experience: Currently pursuing a degree or certificate in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics or a related area discipline. Proficiency in Python or Go and strong software development skills shown through coursework, personal projects and internships. Curiosity about LLMs and a willingness to experiment: you’ve at least tried building with a model API and thought about how it could be manipulated. Experience with security tooling such as Burp Suite, Semgrep, fuzzing frameworks, or Metasploit. Hands-on exploration of prompt injection or jailbreak techniques. Clear communication, especially in writing - you can explain a technical finding to someone who has to fix it. Experience with GitHub and AWS. PID: P79247 Pay Transparency Notice: Depending on your work location, the target hourly rate for this position can range as detailed below. Hourly Rate: $60 — $60 USD Application Limit: Candidates may submit a maximum of 3 applications within a 6-month period. Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information. Applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. jobs.title: Bioinformatics Scientist (Oncology Product Development)
jobs.description: Natera is currently seeking a Bioinformatics Scientist to join the Bioinformatics team focused on Oncology Product Development. The individual will participate in the design and prototyping of cutting-edge algorithms for analysis of genetic data and the development and validation of ctDNA-based diagnostic tests. The ideal candidate will be an enthusiastic, flexible team member with a strong background in bioinformatics and data science, optimally with experience in the analysis or modeling of DNA methylation data. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Analyze next-generation sequencing data ranging from single research experiments to commercial datasets containing hundreds of thousands of samples. Develop Python software infrastructure to support algorithm testing and simulation studies. Produce correct conclusions based on rigorous mathematical analysis and principles of statistics and probability. Contribute to product development and validation efforts in the Bioinformatics group. Drive rigorous data analysis efforts and support group efforts in the production of high-quality documentation. QUALIFICATIONS: Requirements: Master’s degree or PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, engineering, statistics, or a related field; Bachelor’s degree with 2+ years of relevant experience will be considered. At least 2 years of hands-on experience in statistical analysis of biological data using Python or R; analysis of high-throughput genomic sequencing data is preferred. Desirable, but not required: Prior experience analyzing or modeling DNA methylation data. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Experience using Python or R for scientific data analysis and visualization. Strong foundation in statistical modeling/machine learning, including probability theory and estimation/classification methods. Experience with analysis of next-generation sequencing data, preferably including algorithm performance evaluation. Experience with analysis and visualization of complex datasets. Proven ability to apply mathematical principles to solve real estimation problems and implement practical solutions. Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the desire to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $101,800 — $127,300 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @ natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes. For more information: - BBB announcement on job scams - FBI Cyber Crime resource page

cold_email.subject: Interest in Bioinformatics Scientist (Oncology Product Development) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Bioinformatics Scientist (Oncology Product Development) opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Software Engineer - 2027 Start Dates — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Veeva Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Software Engineer - 2027 Start Dates opportunity with Veeva at Veeva.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Staff, Regulatory Affairs Specialist
jobs.description: Staff Regulatory Affairs Specialist About the Role The Staff Regulatory Affairs Specialist plays a key role in advancing the regulatory success of Natera in the fields of women's health, oncology, and organ transplantation worldwide. Working within a team of regulatory professionals and alongside project teams, you will prepare the regulatory submissions required to market new or modified in vitro diagnostic devices in domestic and international clinical markets, and contribute to the development and implementation of regulatory strategies across Natera's products and services. You will bring established technical knowledge and an understanding of regulatory requirements in at least one area of regional expertise (e.g., US FDA, CAP/CLIA/NYS, EU, Japan, or China), and you will grow into additional areas to support the approval, registration, and licensure of Natera's products and services. You will plan, coordinate, and report on regulatory projects of low to moderate complexity, recommend appropriate actions on regulatory issues, and escalate more complex matters to RA leadership. You will serve as a core team member for assigned projects and product lines, collaborating with project teams to ensure the product development process, including clinical studies, addresses regulatory requirements and business objectives. You will also represent the RA team to internal and external stakeholders, provide regulatory analysis and impact assessments on legislation and industry guidance, and maintain product registrations, change assessments, post-market surveillance reports, laboratory licenses, and records of communication with regulatory authorities. cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Staff, Regulatory Affairs Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate 1 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate 1 opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Risk & Monitoring Analyst III
jobs.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions Risk & Monitoring Analyst III As a Risk & Monitoring Analyst III, you'll join the Risk & Controls team, which is responsible for conducting QA audits on Transaction Monitoring alerts across Coinbase's CX and Compliance production teams. You'll audit TMS and KYC-related activity to identify opportunities that improve programmatic execution, from procedural updates and analyst training to metrics creation and check-and-challenge reviews. Your insights will flow directly into feedback loops that strengthen how Coinbase detects and responds to financial crime. What you'll do: Execute weekly QA audit allocations on complex TMS and KYC cases, performing detailed error analysis and documenting findings with clear, actionable recommendations for production teams. Conduct root cause analysis on audit findings, identifying procedural gaps, recurring themes, and knowledge gaps across CX and Financial Crime Compliance teams to drive targeted upskilling and process improvements. Build and deliver QA metrics, insights, and data-driven recommendations to Client Service Management, using trend analysis and impact assessment to prioritize the highest-value improvements. Partner with Data Analytics, Operations, Financial Crime Compliance, and L&D teams to launch or enhance processes, workflows, and training programs based on QA findings. Design and refine QA rubrics, frameworks, and scoring methodologies to ensure consistent, scalable audit standards across compliance operations. Lead improvement projects end-to-end, from impact analysis and stakeholder alignment through execution and measurement, ensuring outcomes are delivered on time and to quality standards. Required Skills and Experience: 4+ years of hands-on experience executing QA, audit, or compliance testing programs across financial services, with working knowledge of BSA/AML laws, regulations, and rules. Experience working across multiple AML systems and programs (e.g., KYC, AML, EDD, TMS, sanctions), with the ability to audit complex cases and identify systemic control gaps. Demonstrated track record developing compliance metrics and reporting, with intermediate-to-advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and PowerPoint/Google Slides. Proven ability to conduct root cause analysis, translate findings into procedural improvements, and collaborate cross-functionally with global partners across CX, compliance, analytics, and L&D. Experience managing projects from scoping through delivery, with a track record of meeting quality standards and deadlines in a fast-paced compliance environment. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. jobs.location: Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY
jobs.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the Team & Role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. Robinhood has been tapped as the brokerage and initial trustee for Government Products, and is working alongside BNY and The U.S. Department of Treasury to develop and operate the program, which aims to expand market access for the next generation of Americans. In this role, you will help build a world-class, intuitive platform, leveraging Robinhood's industry-leading financial technology to deliver a standalone web and app experience for this historic national initiative. The Government Products team focuses on building and scaling systems that support long-term investing and account management for millions of customers. This team works closely with product, data, and infrastructure partners to deliver reliable, secure, and intuitive experiences. You will help shape systems that enable customers to plan for their financial future with confidence! As a Software Engineer, Web , you will be an important contributor to this 0-to-1 initiative. You will be responsible for building the polished, reliable, and accessible customer-facing web experiences that families use to open and manage accounts, and for helping set the patterns of a brand-new front-end codebase. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role where you will directly shape a platform built to serve millions of future customers This role is based in our New York, NY and Menlo Park, CA offices, with in-person attendance expected 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What You'll Do Build, test, and ship web features using React and modern JavaScript for a brand-new, standalone product optimized for security, reliability, and scale. Partner closely with Product, Design, and backend engineers to translate requirements into intuitive, reliable, and accessible customer experiences. Integrate front-end experiences with our backend-for-frontend layer and the services behind it. Contribute to front-end architecture, reusable components, and engineering best practices for a new codebase. Participate in code reviews and help maintain quality, performance, and accessibility across the web experience. What You Bring Experience building production web applications with React and modern JavaScript, with a focus on performance, accessibility, and a polished customer experience. Comfort working with APIs and collaborating closely with backend engineers to deliver end-to-end features. Willingness to learn quickly and navigate ambiguity in a zero-to-one product space. A habit of writing clean, well-tested code, and a strong desire to learn from feedback and grow as an engineer. Clear communication skills with the ability to partner closely with Product, Design, and cross-functional teammates. Experience with financial products or investment technology is a plus. jobs.title: Patient Coordinator
jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: The Organ Health Patient Coordinator (PC) is the primary point of contact and dedicated advocate for patients undergoing organ health genetic testing. This role sits at the heart of Natera's mission — ensuring that every patient is supported, informed, and guided with care through each step of their testing journey. This position will be focused on growing the relationship between Natera and its patients to ensure timely management of testing. Organ Health patients may require a single test or ongoing, long-term monitoring — in either case, the relationships PCs build are essential, whether that means earning the trust of a new patient to complete their first draw or maintaining continuity with patients throughout a recurring testing journey. A natural drive to overcome objections and convert hesitant patients into confident ones is key to growing the business and ensuring no patient is left behind. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Serve as the patient's dedicated advocate and single point of contact for all things related to their Organ Health testing experience. Assess the needs of patients with a focus on customer support, coordination of logistics, and problem solving. Set accurate expectations around sample collection scheduling, turnaround time, billing, and next steps to ensure patients feel informed and confident. Respond to patient-generated marketing leads and conduct outbound outreach for applicable patient identification and monitoring programs. Appropriately triage and escalate complex issues to cross-functional partners including the MP Team, Organ Health Specialists (OHS/Sales), Territory Managers, Customer Experience, and Billing Teams. Participate in rotating weekend on-call coverage to ensure urgent patient needs are addressed in a timely manner. Maintain and support a service-oriented relationship with patients Ensure all data and analysis requests from different parts of the organization are addressed in a timely manner. Identify, nurture and grow patient relationships in order to influence and schedule ongoing testing. Performs other duties as assigned. This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job. Adhere strictly to HIPAA regulations, including verifying patient identity on every interaction conducted. Employees must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire. Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements. QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum of 2 years of Call Center experience in an inbound and outbound capacity, patient services, or healthcare customer support role. Minimum of 2 years of sales experience Background in medical or biological sciences preferred KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Genuine empathy and compassion; Strong active listening and rapport-building skills with the ability to handle emotionally complex conversations professionally. jobs.title: Customer Engineer
jobs.description: ABOUT US: AI NEEDS A NEW INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. WE'RE BUILDING IT AT MODAL. Every era of computing brought new workloads that previous infrastructure couldn't support: mainframes, databases, and the cloud. Each time, the company that rebuilt the layer underneath defined the decade. AI is no different, except it touches everything instead of one slice, and the window to build the layer underneath it is open right now. Our customers include category-defining companies like Ramp https://modal.com/blog/how-ramp-built-a-full-context-background-coding-agent-on-modal, Cognition, DoorDash, and Suno. They rely on Modal for instant GPU access, sub-second container starts, and native storage, so it's simple to serve low-latency inference, fine-tune models, and access production-ready sandboxes at scale. We've passed $1B in annualized run rate, up 15x from a year ago. In October 2026 we raised a $750M Series D led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation. Our team includes creators of popular open-source projects (e.g., Seaborn https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn, Luigi https://github.com/spotify/luigi), academic researchers, international olympiad medalists, and experienced engineering and product leaders with decades of experience. THE ROLE: We're looking for engineers with deep AI/ML and low-level systems experience who want to build the best technical support experience in the world. This isn't a traditional support role — it's an engineering role where you happen to be closest to our customers. You'll split your time roughly 50/50 between working directly with customers and shipping fixes, features, and automation that improve Modal for everyone. When you help a customer debug a training run, you'll also fix the underlying issue in the platform. When you notice ten customers hitting the same friction point, you'll build the tooling or automation that eliminates it entirely. This role is for people who solve problems, not people who answer tickets. The problems you encounter are deeply technical and arise from running some of the most demanding AI workloads in the world. You'll be a member of our engineering team, contributing production code alongside the engineers building the core platform. The difference is that your roadmap is shaped by what you learn at the frontier of customer experience. You will: - Ship code that matters. Fix bugs, build features, and create automation that improves the experience for every Modal user — not just the one who reported the issue. - Work directly with customers. Help developers and ML engineers debug, optimize, and architect their workloads across Slack, email, and calls. - Build scalable systems. Design tooling, dashboards, and automated workflows that make support efficient at scale — delighting customers at the most important moments. - Close the feedback loop. Translate patterns you see in the field into concrete improvements — docs fixes, API changes, or new feature proposals. - Contribute to open source and technical content. Write examples, build demos, and publish content that helps the broader community succeed on Modal. REQUIREMENTS: - Accomplished in key areas. You bring depth in either low-level infrastructure or ML/AI, and you're not lost in the other. - Low-level infrastructure experience. Operating systems, file systems, networking, performance profiling, cluster management and distributed systems. - AI/ML engineering experience. Training models, optimizing inference, working with GPUs, or building ML infrastructure. - Automation mindset. Your instinct when you see a manual process is to eliminate it and you have the engineering background to make that happen. - Clear communicator. Can explain a systems issue to a customer, write a crisp bug report, and draft documentation, all while collaborating internally to ship improvements.

jobs.description: ABOUT FORMATION BIO Formation Bio is a tech and AI driven pharma company differentiated by radically more efficient drug development. Advancements in AI and drug discovery are creating more candidate drugs than the industry can progress because of the high cost and time of clinical trials. Recognizing that this development bottleneck may ultimately limit the number of new medicines that can reach patients, Formation Bio, founded in 2016 as TrialSpark Inc., has built technology platforms, processes, and capabilities to accelerate all aspects of drug development and clinical trials. Formation Bio partners, acquires, or in-licenses drugs from pharma companies, research organizations, and biotechs to develop programs past clinical proof of concept and beyond, ultimately helping to bring new medicines to patients. The company is backed by investors across pharma and tech, including a16z, Sequoia, Sanofi, Thrive Capital, John Doerr, Spark Capital, SV Angel Growth, and others. You can read more at the following links: - Our Vision for AI in Pharma https://www.formation.bio/blog/our-vision-for-ai-in-pharma - Our Current Drug Portfolio https://www.formation.bio/licensing-and-pipeline - Our Technology & Platform https://www.formation.bio/technology At Formation Bio, our values are the driving force behind our mission to revolutionize the pharma industry. Every team and individual at the company shares these same values, and every team and individual plays a key part in our mission to bring new treatments to patients faster and more efficiently. About the Position Clinical trials are the slowest and most expensive stage of bringing a new medicine to patients, and most sponsors still run them much as they did twenty years ago. The Trial Engine is how Formation Bio runs trials instead, with small teams supported by technology tools and AI systems that handle much of the work that would otherwise require a large operations staff. We develop it alongside its use in our own studies. As the primary product manager for the Trial Engine, you will shape its product strategy with clinical and technology leadership. You will develop a clear point of view on where Formation can make the biggest improvements, challenge assumptions about how trials should run, and inform which ideas deserve investment. This is a hands-on role. You will build and test early versions of tools, agents, and workflows yourself, work directly with the people running our studies, and use what you learn to sharpen the strategy. Once a direction is set, you are responsible for getting it into use, which in a GxP environment means working through quality review, vendor management, site requirements, and established practice. Our 2027 portfolio includes several new studies across active programs, and we are building these capabilities in parallel to run them more efficiently. Your work will connect the needs of our next studies to a longer-term plan for capabilities that become more useful with each trial. If you're a strong PM looking for a step up, this is a rare seat: high scope, direct exposure to senior clinical and technology leaders, and a chance to shape a problem space that most of the industry hasn't touched yet. Responsibilities - Shape the Trial Engine product strategy with clinical and technology leadership. Develop a clear point of view on how Formation should use AI, software, and changes to how teams work to run trials more effectively. - Lead the development roadmap for the Trial Engine capabilities, including what is built, what is deferred, and how success is measured against trial timelines, cost, and staff effort. - For each problem, determine whether the right solution is custom software, an AI agent, a process change, a vendor, or a manual workflow. - Develop a working understanding of clinical operations, data management, monitoring, and site management, with enough depth to see where time and cost actually accumulate in a study. - Build and test first versions of workflows, tools, and agents yourself using AI tools and our internal platforms. Evaluate them against representative trial tasks and data, investigate failures, and use what you learn to guide further investment. - Take capabilities from concept to use on an active trial, working with Engineering, Development Operations, Quality, Regulatory, and external vendors, and resolve the obstacles that arise along the way. - Understand GCP, computer system validation, and our SDLC well enough to recognize GxP implications early and involve QA and validation partners at the right stage. - Own rollout, training, and user feedback. A capability is complete once the trial team depends on it in their daily work; capabilities that are not being used should be reworked or retired. - Establish baselines for the work being addressed, and track whether each capability shortens time to trial milestones or reduces manual effort. About You - Three to six years in product management, product operations, strategy, consulting, or a comparable role in which you owned outcomes and made prioritization decisions with incomplete information. - A strong, reasoned point of view. You form your own judgment, identify opportunities beyond incoming requests, and constructively challenge established approaches. You can defend your reasoning and change your mind when the evidence changes. - Strong prioritization judgment. Given a long list of requests, you can identify the few that matter, and you are as willing to conclude that a problem does not need software as you are to argue for a new build. - A fast learner: you don't need clinical trial experience, but you can get up to speed on a complex, regulated domain quickly and you enjoy doing it. Prior exposure to life sciences, healthcare, or another regulated industry is a plus. - Relentless follow-through: you've pushed work through organizations with competing priorities, skeptical stakeholders, and real constraints. - A hands-on builder. You can show tools, agents, or workflows you personally built, explain how they work and where they fail, and describe how feedback improved them. - Enough technical depth to work credibly with engineers. You can discuss trade-offs, review a design document, and recognize when a proposed solution is more complex than the problem requires. - Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain a prioritization decision to clinical operations, quality, and engineering audiences in terms that each finds convincing. - Comfort with ambiguity. The roadmap will shift as the portfolio changes, and you will help define the team's scope as it develops. Total Compensation Range: $185,500 - $232,000 Compensation Individual compensation is determined by several factors, including role scope, geographic location, and skills & experience. Your offer will reflect where you fall within the range based on these considerations. In addition to base salary, we offer equity, comprehensive benefits, and generous perks. If the posted range doesn't match your expectations, we still encourage you to apply! Where We Hire Formation Bio is prioritizing hiring in key hubs, primarily the New York City and Boston metro areas, with a hybrid model requiring 3 days per week in office. cold_email.subject: Interest in Customer Marketing Manager — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Cognition Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Customer Marketing Manager opportunity with Cognition at Cognition.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Clinical Oncology Specialist, Head & Neck
jobs.description: LOCATION: The territory for this position includes Northern California. Join Natera's Head & Neck Oncology histology team as a Clinical Oncology Specialist (COS). In this high-impact, field-based role, you will drive the adoption and growth of Signatera, Natera's personalized molecular residual disease (MRD) ctDNA assay, helping clinicians monitor cancer and inform treatment decisions throughout the patient journey. As a trusted clinical and commercial partner, you will build strategic relationships with key stakeholders across academic medical centers, integrated delivery networks, hospital systems, and community oncology practices. You will collaborate cross-functionally to expand access to Signatera while partnering with Radiation Oncologists, ENT/Otolaryngology physicians, Head & Neck Surgeons, Medical Oncologists, Pathologists, and other members of the multidisciplinary care team. We are looking for a relationship-driven sales professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment. This role requires frequent travel throughout the assigned territory. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Develop expertise in Natera's oncology portfolio, clinical data, reimbursement landscape, competitive positioning, and internal processes. Identify and develop relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), academic medical centers, hospital systems, and community oncology practices to drive adoption of Natera's oncology portfolio. Engage H&N oncologists and other healthcare professionals through consultative, clinical discussions that support the adoption of Natera's oncology diagnostics. Develop and execute strategic territory plans to identify growth opportunities and influence key clinical and administrative stakeholders. Achieve sales objectives and drive growth within the assigned territory. Maintain accurate territory activity, customer insights, and sales forecasts while identifying risks and new business opportunities. Conduct all business activities with integrity while maintaining compliance with company policies and industry regulations. Perform other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree required. 5+ years of successful medical sales experience, preferably within Head & Neck Oncology, Medical Oncology, Surgical Oncology, molecular diagnostics, or precision medicine. Knowledge of the academic and community oncology landscape, including molecular diagnostics, precision medicine, and reimbursement. Experience calling on Radiation Oncologists, ENT/Otolaryngology physicians, Head & Neck Surgeons, Medical Oncologists, or other Head & Neck oncology stakeholders preferred. Demonstrated leadership, business acumen, financial management, and strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability and willingness to travel overnight as needed. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to build trusted relationships and influence physicians, key opinion leaders, and multidisciplinary healthcare teams. Strategic thinker with strong business acumen and the ability to develop and execute territory growth strategies. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. Ability to communicate complex clinical and scientific information effectively to diverse healthcare audiences. Demonstrated ability to work independently while collaborating across cross-functional teams. Knowledge of oncology market dynamics, molecular diagnostics, precision medicine, and healthcare reimbursement is preferred. The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. On-target earnings (OTE) represent the total potential income an employee can earn by achieving 100% of their performance goals. It combines a base salary with commissions and serves as an estimated figure rather than a guaranteed amount, providing a guideline based on average performance outcomes. On-target earnings (OTE) $225,000 — $230,000 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @ natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes. For more information: - BBB announcement on job scams - FBI Cyber Crime resource page

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Oncology Specialist, Head & Neck — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Oncology Specialist, Head & Neck opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.description: WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS. We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer. Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro. Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us. WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS. We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer, and Windsurf, the AI-native IDE. Together, they represent our vision for collaborative AI teammates that enable engineers to focus on more interesting problems and empower teams to strive for more ambitious goals. Our team is small and talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro. Building Devin and Windsurf is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us. ABOUT THE ROLE At Cognition, customers are our highest priority. Deployed Engineers (DEs) are customer-facing technical experts who help our customers maximize the value they get out of Devin/Windsurf. You’ll work directly with engineers to understand their workflows, identify high-impact use cases, and deploy Devin/Windsurf into real production environments. You’ll lead demos and pilots, support integrations, and drive adoption of the Cognition platform from the inside out. This role combines hands-on technical work, customer partnership, and rapid execution. You'll serve a broad range of clients, switching context frequently and staying ahead of issues before they become blockers. You're expected to be proactive, make judgment calls, and take ownership of outcomes. In this role, you will: - Own all technical aspects of the customer lifecycle—from deployment through activation, making sure our customers are successful using Devin - Work closely with customers to understand their technical challenges and identify the best use cases for Devin to be a productive contributor - Build deep relationships with our customers’ engineering teams to ensure smooth product integration and adoption, activating top users and driving product utilization - Build! Always listen to customer feedback, have a bias towards implementing requested features yourself, and advocate for the customers’ needs with the rest of the team - Be the customer oracle! Exercise your product instincts to help set the roadmap What We Value - Customer empathy — you care deeply about how engineers work and what helps them succeed - Ownership mindset — you take responsibility for results, not just tasks - Technical curiosity — you enjoy digging into unfamiliar systems and understanding how they really work - Bias toward execution — you move quickly from problem to solution - Grit — you’re comfortable operating in ambiguous, high-intensity environments - Exploratory rigor — You poke at edges, ask uncomfortable questions, and would rather find problems yourself than have them find you. Requirements - Strong engineering foundation from a rigorous technical environment - Demonstrated track record of exceptional performance in whatever you've pursued, whether academic, athletic, professional, or entrepreneurial - Self-directed by default. You don't need a manager to tell you what to do next or how to prioritize. - Strong communication skills. You can hold your own with senior engineers and executives alike. - Have a high tolerance for ambiguity, intensity, and sustained effort when the problem demands it. - Willingness to travel across MENA - 50% You might excel if you… - Advanced in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, TypeScript) - Experience writing and debugging real software systems - Want to work directly with real users on high-impact technical problems - Learn quickly by being embedded in challenging, real-world environments - Have worked at an early-stage startup or in a role where you operated well beyond your job description OUR COMMITMENT Equal Opportunity. Cognition is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process - please let us know if you need any. Cognition also considers applicants with criminal histories consistent with the SF Fair Chance Ordinance and similar local laws. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Celina Lin
